**No** — `CatalogApi.CreateItem` does not publish `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` (or any integration event).

What `CreateItem` does, exactly (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:366-388`):
1. Constructs a new `CatalogItem` from the posted `product`, copying `Id`, `CatalogBrandId`, `CatalogTypeId`, `Description`, `PictureFileName`, `Price`, `AvailableStock`, `RestockThreshold`, and `MaxStockThreshold` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:370-381`).
2. Computes and assigns an AI embedding for the item via `services.CatalogAI.GetEmbeddingAsync(item)` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:382`).
3. Adds the item to `services.Context.CatalogItems` and calls `SaveChangesAsync()` — a plain EF Core save, with no `EventService` usage (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:384-385`).
4. Returns `TypedResults.Created($"/api/catalog/items/{item.Id}")` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:387`).

It is registered as `POST /items` (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:103-104`).

How I established this: a repo-wide search for `ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent` returned only one publishing site in Catalog.API, and it is in `UpdateItem`, not `CreateItem` — it fires only when the EF price property is modified (`src/Catalog.API/Apis/CatalogApi.cs:347-357`), using `SaveEventAndCatalogContextChangesAsync` then `PublishThroughEventBusAsync`. The other matches are the event record definitions (`src/Catalog.API/IntegrationEvents/Events/ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent.cs:6`, `src/Webhooks.API/IntegrationEvents/ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEvent.cs:3`) and its subscriber in Webhooks.API (`src/Webhooks.API/Extensions/Extensions.cs:21`, `src/Webhooks.API/IntegrationEvents/ProductPriceChangedIntegrationEventHandler.cs:3-5`).
